items.title: Use of Indigenous-Themed Names, Logos and Images within or on
notes: Township Facilities and Properties Policy
Report from K.Bettiol, Manager of Community Development K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development provided an overview of the report
outlining the background and various phases undertaken to the reconciliation-focused policy pathway to respectful indigenous representation. She
outlined the key points from the draft policy as follows:
• no new indigenous-themed imagery may be introduced by non- indigenous groups;
• existing imagery (banners) may be reinstalled, but only with appropriate
• historical and cultural context and permanent contextual display;
• emphasis on education, transparency and reconciliation through public communication and training;.
• establish a framework for respectful and inclusive representation going forward.
K. Bettiol highlighted the plans for the contextual display, including the location and the
specific wording of the display and introduced the art work of Kory Parkin. She
explained the next steps that include: 1) re-installation of the banners with the
permanent contextual display, 2) Establish the education components of the
reconciliation-focused policy pathway to respectful indigenous representation; 3) build
out the webpage linked to the display’s QR code.
Artist Kory Parkin provided an overview and background on the permanent contextual
Display and shared the inspiration for his artwork.

Councillor MacDonald, having declared a conflict of interest regarding the 2026 Community Investment Fund Recommendations, left the Council Chamber and therefore did not participate in the discussions or vote on the matter.

items.title: Stormwater Management Facility By-law
notes: Report from G. Atkinson, Manager of Wastewater Services Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services provided an overview of the report, indicating the purpose of the by-law is to outline what is and is not allowed to occur in the storm water management facilities. He noted enforcement of the by-law will assist in protecting public safety as stormwater management ponds and channels may look harmless, but often have deep water, sudden drop-offs, slippery banks or fast-moving flow.
C. Baker responded to questions regarding invasive species in storm water management facilities and the plan to undertake an education and awareness campaign.

items.title: Downtown Elora Traffic Study
notes: Report from E. Alessio, Engineering Technologist - Transportation Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services introduced Trevor Brown, the new Manager of Engineering and Public Works.

Ryan Maiden, Supervisor of Capital Projects and Transportation provided an overview of the report, indicating staff is recommending a study be completed to assess current traffic conditions in the downtown core and provide strategies to address congestion.

In response to questions, R. Maiden explained the project, led by the Township, will be completed in partnership with the County of Wellington. The project budget is $100,000 with Wellington County contributing $50,000 of the funding and the Township contributing $50,000. Staff responded to additional questions regarding the fall 2025 study undertaken by the County and the recommendations to be implemented, the timing and scope of the project.
